The Michelson programming language is being utilized for the development of Ethereum-compatible smart contracts, and ensuring correctness during the programming process is being enhanced through static analysis tools, including the HELMHOLTZ tool. We present a significant advancement to the existing HELMHOLTZ framework, specifically in its capability to detect overflow and underflow vulnerabilities for integer operations within Michelson programs. This improvement involves a new set of Michelson compilers and a revised flow domain in the resulting property graphs, specifically introducing the 'nonzero' flow. As a result, HELMHOLTZ can now identify low-level numerical over/underflows via the 'nonzero' overflow underflow property queries, and we have demonstrated this enhancement with the re-analysis of 13 successfully exploited Michelson-based contracts. We showcase an example of a newly discovered overflow bug in the Tezos Treasury smart contract as part of the Global Tezos Security Audit 2019.

It has been shown that modern Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures, 
which combine 1D/2D/3D Convolutional and fully connected (FC) layers, are equivalent 
to specific graph-based CNNs on predetermined graph structures for certain data 
representation and processing tasks. We have demonstrated that zero-initialized 
Convolutional and FC layers can be viewed as a graph convolution and max-aggregation 
operation on hypernodes, respectively. We have also confirmed this hypothesis 
through experiments that reveal the actual operation performed by current CNN 
architectures matches that of GCNs on hypergraphs. Building on this discovery, we 
propose Hypergraph Convolutional Neural Networks (HCNNs) as a flexible framework 
incorporating zero-initialized Convolutional and FC layers, and demonstrate its 
robustness and adaptability when compared to established CNN models. HCNNs achieve 
competitive performance in both transductive and inducible node classification 
tasks while requiring less learning parameters, and we found that pre-training 
HCNNs and gradually reducing their learning rate leads to improved performance.

We investigate a one-loop correction to the entropy of rotating "hairy" black holes, in the context of 3D gravity with CS modification, and find that it aligns with the area-based formula $S=A/4$.  By comparing this result to the one found in standard CS theory, we uncover a additional term, which can be expressed as the difference between the "hairy" and standard black hole entropies at the horizon, and we propose that this indicates the entropy of the "hairy" black holes is unaffected by their angular momentum.  To validate this, we provide a path integral derivation of the entropy, employing the replica trick, and confirm that it matches the result from semiclassical analysis.  However, this derivation relies on the choice of the CS level, in units of Planck's constant, in the high temperature limit.  A similar correction to the entropy is derived for the "hairy" black holes in the AdS$_{5}$ case with a cubic derivative correction to the action, and we demonstrate that it aligns with the holographic c-theorem, implying that the entropy of the "hairy" black holes is less than that of the standard AdS black holes.  We also provide a derivation of the entropy using the J/T method from the field theory side.

A novel method is presented for deriving the fusion rules of non-invertible symmetries, even when their charges cannot be directly observed. By leveraging the categorical duality between non-invertible symmetry algebras and defect lines, a relationship is established between the fusion rule trace and defect line correlation, building upon the Osterwalder-Schroder equality that equates their factors. This approach enables the derivation of previously unknown fusion rules, such as those for the Amplitudine defect in a model of electron mean-field spin-1/2 lattice and the Amplitudine defect auto-fusion in 2d Ising conformal field theory.

The quantitative lateral and axial displacement estimation in ultrasound elastography (UE) hold significant clinical value, with the axial direction's accuracy surpassing that of the lateral direction. Accurate axial strain and modulus mapping are primarily limited by the precision of axial displacement estimation, whereas lateral displacement estimation's inaccuracy is constrained by accurate axial displacement estimation. Traditional cross-correlation methods are employed for 1D axial and lateral displacement estimation but are hindered by sampling theory, resulting in inaccuracies. Consequently, it becomes necessary to employ a high-resolution interpolation method for 1D measurements. This research integrates a robust traditional 1D cross-correlation (1D-CO) measurement with a high-resolution interpolation (HRI) algorithm to enhance lateral and axial displacement measurements in UE. The proposed algorithm compares its results to those of a traditional 2D coherent propagation sampling (2D-CPS) algorithm, a renowned ultrafast UE frame acquisition and processing framework, utilizing high-quality phantom and in vivo data sets. Findings indicate that the proposed algorithm's lateral and axial displacement measurements are nearly identical to that of the 2D-CPS algorithm, whereas traditional 1D measurements deviate notably in the lateral direction.

Pseudocodes play a vital role in the communication between people who design high-level system abstractions and those who implement them.
Traditionally, pseudocodes have been used to clarify the correctness and usability of these designs by providing a verifiable format.
However, current methods of correctness checking depend on formal languages that are both costly and time-consuming to parse.
To address this issue, we introduce logical pseudocodes, a novel concept extending pseudocodes with logic, which are machine-checkable without the need for formal parsing.
These logical pseudocodes ensure that the intended correctness and safety properties of the algorithm are guaranteed, while also being easily implementable in any existing programming language.
To demonstrate the practicality and efficiency of this idea, we created a tool called logical-c, an open-source over-approximative static analysis framework based on logical pseudocodes written in C-like code.
Our initial experiments indicate that logical pseudocodes can provide precise correctness verification for substantial codebases, bringing these abstractions much closer to being practically usable.

Given a positive integer $k$ and an ordering of the elements in $2^{k}$, a coloring is called rainbowed if no subset of $2^{k}$ of any size is colored with multiple colors. This work explores the Boolean rainbow Ramsey number $br(k)$, a threshold at which there exists a non-rainbow coloring using $br(k)$ or more colors. Previous studies have investigated $br(k)$ for small values of $k$, and this paper extends that research by increasing $k$ up to 8, and discussing results for $k$ up to 10.

We developed an efficient, non-iterative coreset creation method for the $k$-means clustering problem under a general distance measure. By processing the data in a single pass and using random sampling, our algorithm achieves a coarse solution within a fixed time. Notably, our method uses around $\tilde{O}(\min \{mk, n\})$ more data than the optimal $k$-means cost. We improved a previous coarser algorithm by using a linear projection to reduce the coarser coreset, resulting in an more accurate coarser coreset.

This research paper focuses on cooperative pursuit-evasion tasks within grid worlds, specifically in scenario where multiple pursuers aim to capture a single evader. Building upon our previous work with hierarchical A* for 2-pplayer grid worlds, we expand our methodology by applying hierarchical A* to larger, multi-player grid worlds. By reorganizing the state space into distinct sections, each with its own dynamic model, we create a framework that breaks down the complex scenario into manageable parts. This adaptive hierarchical approach not only identifies the optimal solution by analyzing the superstates created from the grid's partition, but also provides a crucial pathway for scaling up tasks of this nature. We validate our method through numerical experiments, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency.

A set of probability distributions $\mathcal{P}_k$ for $k$-tuples in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is defined, and specific applications are explored including nonextensive entropy, optimal transportation costs, and tail expectations. A criterion is established to determine when a $k$-tuple within $\mathcal{P}_k$ exhibits nonextensive, optimal transportation, or heavy-tailed characteristics. It is also demonstrated that single-component distributions can exhibit nonextensive behavior even when being the combination of multiple independent light-tailed components. Furthermore, subsets of $\mathcal{uk}$ and $\mathcal{max}_k$ are identified, and the conditions to classify a $k$-tuple within these subsets are specified.

This research proposes an enhanced version of the cycleGAN architecture, where the AdaIN technique is employed for adaptive feature modulation in the generator. The modifications enable the architecture to eliminate the need for unidirectional data flow, allowing for complete data separation by two feature2image generators. The AdaIN technique's adaptability to input variations gives the architecture excellent generalization capabilities. The proposed method, AdaCycleGAN, achieves state-of-the-art results in rain removal tasks, delivering high-fidelity results with enhanced details compared to other cycle-consistent GAN approaches. The model exhibits exceptional performance even with limited clear images for training, exhibiting less over-smoothing than competing methods. AdaCycleGAN also excels in ground detection tasks, outperforming other cycle-consistent GAN designs. The achieved results demonstrate the efficacy of AdaIN in enhancing the performance of the generator. To further enhance the architecture, possible extensions are discussed.

In this research, we analyze the use of multi-view representation learning in dialog systems and impact scoring on the training of representations. We examine a specific dialog scoring task, where users express preferences towards friends they're considering to be with. First, we propose a new score calculation method that takes into account various factors, including the user's stated preference, the appeal of the friends, and the proximity of the location. This proves crucial in representing the users' desires accurately. Without this, the training process fails to achieve the desired results. To tackle the issue, we suggest a simple yet effective approach using contrastive learning to enhance the score calculation method. Our experiments show that this can lead to significant improvements in performance.

In this research, a second-order differential equation resulting from the combination of the potential vector field and a specific soliton equation is examined, after which its implications lead to a modified version of the Laplace equation, known as the YL equation. Furthermore, we derive a first integrable form of the YL equation.

For deformed halos, a novel approach is presented within the context of the shell model, featuring flexibility to address both static and dynamic halos. By applying this model to the neutron halos of $^{11}$Li and $^{6}$He, we determined the ground, low-lying excited states and certain collective states for both cases. The findings show that quasi 1p$h_{2/3/5/2}$-deformed halo configurations result in a compact ground state and specific excited states, while the deformed $1p^{3/2}$ halo configurations lead to a diffuse ground state. Furthermore, quasi proton spherically deformed core states were discovered using this model. The results indicate that the halo's configuration directly impacts its shape, and the model successfully describes both static and dynamic halos.

One key limitation of BasicVSR is its use of extensive computational complexity in cross-layer attention modules, which hampers its practical applications. BasicVsr++ addresses this issue by introducing a single, efficient attention module that significantly reduces computational demands, resulting in a substantial improvement in efficiency. Compared to BasicVSR, pvrs++ achieves a notable decrease in computational complexity ($4.5\times$) and memory demands ($2.25\times$), while matching or surpassing it in accuracy. Specifically, pvrs++ achieves almost the same visual results as BasicVSR with only $0.9222$ PSNR difference on the testing set, while offering a significant improvement in efficiency.

This study addresses the challenge of describing parton distribution functions (PDFs) for W and Z bosons in the context of high-energy collisions.  A perturbation theoretic analysis is used to examine the relevant subprocesses at the leading order of quantum chromodynamics (QCD).  It is demonstrated that, at the leading order, the PDFs for W and Z bosons can be expressed in terms of the PDFs for quarks and anti-quarks.  Further analysis reveals that, at higher orders, the relevant correction terms vanish as the distance from the interaction point approaches zero, allowing for factorization of the relevant correction terms into the parton distribution functions (PDFs) with a corresponding factorizing scale.  A calculation of these corrections at next-to-leading order (NLO) is performed, involving both strong electric charge and mass effects.  A comparison with the traditional approach of treating the mass as an intrinsic variable is also made.

Using multiple policies to explore different tasks is a common strategy in multi-task reinforcement learning (MRL). Unfortunately, this approach often suffers from the problem of factorized learning, where there is no communication between the models, resulting in the inability to share useful knowledge and the emergence of conflicting information. To effectively learn both tasks, a shared knowledge model and a mechanism to reconcile conflicting information are crucial. To address these challenges, we introduce a new model called Factorized Learning with Attention and Shared Communication, where attention learning enables the exchange of useful information between the models, and shared communication learns simultaneously with factorized learning during the training process. Our method is built on top of a multi-head framework and involves introducing a shared communication module and a attention learning module. To further improve the quality of information exchanged, we introduce an information filter. The experimental results show that F-LASC outperforms the current state-of-the-art methods on the Rocket and MiniGrid tasks.

This paper proves that a key property of solutions to a specific type of differential equation, which holds near a compact area, also applies throughout the rest of a noncompact surface, under certain growth conditions. As a result, various alternative versions of a mathematical theorem known as the unique continuation property follow from this finding.

Godel's first incompleteness theorem, reinforced by Rosser's modification, demonstrates that no consistent Peano arithmetic formulation can capture all true statements about natural numbers. This study delves into the origins of Godel's and Rosser's principles within axiomatic Peano arithmetic, exploring their implications on the understanding of incomplete formal systems. By applying a semantic framework to Peano arithmetic, the research suggests that this self-contained system might be circumstantially sufficient to describe all truths about the natural numbers.

This study provides concise proofs of the two-dimensional version of Hadamard's three circles theorem for functions in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\mathbb{R}^n$. For functions in $\mathbb{R}^n$, the monogenic property allows the use of the generalized Poisson integral to derive the result, offering a more intuitive understanding. Moreover, this approach can be adapted to address the problem for semigroups of operators that satisfy the property of having contractive semigroups.

When conducting surveys, particularly complex ones, a crucial step involves choosing a balanced random sample from the population. For an extended period, the industry standard for this was the iterative reweighting method to adjust inclusion weights. To refine this process, we introduce a novel algorithm that efficiently selects a balanced sample in a non-iterative way. This new method proves to be as effective as the traditional approach and offers the added advantage of reducing computational time and minimizing the risk of human interference.

Traditionally, various estimation problems from geometry and graphics have been addressed by first deriving a probabilistic model, latent variables, and then optimizing the relevant parameters to find the best match for observed data. While effective, this approach requires marginalizing high-dimensional variables and can be resource-intensive. As an alternative, we explore a direct path to predictions by training a neural network model to output estimates directly, an approach we investigate across three applications: monocular camera calibration, multi-view camera calibration, and structure-from-motion. The results show that our direct method generally matches or surpasses classical methods, even when provided with comparable data, despite the potential for physical models to encode prior knowledge and expertise.

This research applies the conditionally trained WGAN model to compute a posterior that can be evaluated and sampled from, given observed evidence. We propose using the WGAN generator to approximate the posterior distribution, which allows for a flexible representation of complex data distributions and an efficient sampling method. Notably, this approach does not require the posterior to belong to a specific family, enabling more accurate inferences from data that may be non-Gaussian or exhibit correlations. We demonstrate the approach with real medical image data, specifically TLR9 stimulation of monocytes and neutrophils.

This study provides essential criteria for identifying linear subspaces within fractional order systems, mirroring the principles applied to integer order systems. We derive a sufficient condition for invariant subspaces under the Caputo fractional order system. A key formula for the image of a linear subspace, spanned by the column vectors of a matrix, is also established. This formula is inapplicable to the Riemann-Liouville fractional order system due to the absence of initial value assumptions. A different formula is thus essential for both topics.

In this paper, a multi-hop, in-air terahertz communication protocol called COMET is introduced, which utilizes dynamic beam training to optimize link performance. COMET is designed for a system architecture in which each node in the network controls its own transmit and receive beams, in contrast to traditional wired or radio frequency backhaul systems where all nodes share the same beam. To address the challenge of synchronization required for multi-hop links, COMET proposes a time-division multiaccess (TDMA) based scheduling scheme called starline. To demonstrate the flexibility and efficiency of COMET, a time optimization algorithm is developed to allocate time and compute resources in order to minimize delay and consumption. An iterative method with closed-form formulas is used to solve this optimization problem. Numerical simulations show that COMET significantly improves link performance by up to 50% compared to traditional static beam training systems.

The radio pulsar known as the "Pincus" has been studied individually for three decades. Through the "Cameleon" project, we identified 59 separate scattering screens at various distances from Earth. The smallest and largest screens were identified in the 3.5 to 9.5 GHz and 0.4 to 1.6 GHz frequency ranges, respectively. The screen data was used to estimate the amount of plasma in the vicinity of the "Pincus" and found to be consistent with the amount of plasma along the line of sight from Earth to the pulsar. The screen screen distribution appears to be consistent with the expected flux of plasma in the interstellar medium. The most compact screen was located at 2.4 kiloparsecs from Earth, which allowed the "Pincus" to be resolved at 850 MHz, with an estimated size of less than 120 microarcseconds. The findings highlight the need for a sensitive, long baseline array to study the "Pincus" at higher frequencies.

Human speech is a complex, quasi-periodic sound pattern similar to other signals composed of repeating components. In this analysis, a cascaded network was studied as an effective method for modeling such signals by breaking them down into simpler, repeating parts. A cascaded VQ-Transform network was implemented, combining vector quantization and transform modeling stages to better capture both the periodic and unique aspects of speech. This implementation was then evaluated against traditional vector quantization methods and showcase the potential of cascaded networks in creating high-fidelity representations of quasi-periodic signals.

Annotating extensive datasets for NLP tasks, such as linguistic licensing tests, can be both time-consuming and prone to error, especially when done manually. To increase the efficiency of the annotators at the Laboratoire de Linguistique Appliqu\'ee (LLA), we developed a user-friendly web tool called LLA-Ann. This tool LLA-Ann was specifically designed to streamline the annotation process and provide real-time feedback to the annotators. To further enhance the tool's effectiveness, LLA-Ann can be trained on existing datasets, allowing the annotators to receive corrective feedback from the training examples. To evaluate the tool's performance, we developed an algorithm for the creation of high-quality test datasets. Our results show that LLA-Ann significantly improves the speed and accuracy of the annotators, with the tool's feedback providing a noticeable boost in both speed and accuracy.

A new initiative aims to investigate the composition of a diverse range of temperate planets by integrating high-resolution, multi-wavelength data with globally applicable models of the planet's atmosphere. By setting up simulated atmospheric scenarios, the project will assess the ability of a unified analysis to accurately measure the metallicity and temperature of these planets. Using the exoplanet 55 Cancri e as a benchmark, the experiment reveals that the planet's metallicity can be constrained to within a factor of ten, with a corresponding temperature range of 30K. It also indicates that the atmosphere is likely dry due to low levels of H2O. However, the accuracy of these measurements is influenced by the planet's atmospheric properties, particularly the amount of heavy elements found in the atmosphere, which in turn affects the abundance of various gases such as CO, CO2, and NH3. To further refine the model and improve the analysis, additional observations are required in the infrared. In contrast, the approach is less dependent on detailed models of the planet's interior due to the abundance of CO being largely controlled by temperature rather than the amount of oxygen available.

To distinguish true Majorana modes from simulations, we propose using entropy as a diagnostic tool. In our model, the impact of a finite energy splitting due to impurities causes a peak at zero energy in the system's totalization. Notably, this effect vanishes at finite temperatures, where only the influence of thermal fluctuations remains on the entropy of the system's auxiliary part. We show that by applying a fit to the temperature dependence of this entropy, one can extract the value of the energy splitting and thus differentiate genuine Majorana modes from simulations.

Road inspections are crucial, yet time-consuming and labor-intensive, especially when requiring detailed image analysis of road infrastructure. To streamline this process, a combined approach utilizing road tracking and vision-based defect recognition was developed, leveraging two deep learning models, RACON and RoadIns, and a novel data synthesis technique using RoadGenesis. RACON refined an existing road tracking framework, while RoadIns utilized road image generation with roadgens to reduce the need for real training data. To validate this approach, a prototype was created, demonstrating improved inspection efficiency through real-time defect recognition and enhanced accuracy, outperforming traditional methods by 12.75% in F1 score for crack detection.

The primary objective of this study is to formulate a precise definition of topological Hochschild homology (THH) within a bicategorical context and to derive a representability theorem for this bicategorical THH. Building on prior work, this research expands on a natural THH construction for any symmetric monoidal bicategory and its algebras. By incorporating elements from topological algebraic K-theory, this paper introduces a topological version (THH) applicable to any algebra within a symmetric monoidal bicategory. A key finding is that the THH of the algebra $KP$ of a 2-ring $R$ is equivalent to THH of $R$ itself, establishing an interactive relationship between THH and topological algebraic K-theory.

To enhance research in sound classification, especially for complex or recurring sounds like speech, we've created the VGG-Sound Source (VGG-SS) benchmark. This new reference framework is designed for the task of identifying sound sources. It consists of a comprehensive database of 1000 categories and a matching set of test questions. VGG-SS offers a range of identification difficulties and can be used to evaluate the performance of various class numbers. The primary focus of this research is on identifying all 1000 classes. To achieve this, we've evaluated several approaches, resulting in the development of the VGG-Sound Source Network (VGG-SSN). This new network builds upon the VGG-Sound Network (VGG-SN), which was previously used for sound recognition. The VGG-SSN includes a new multi-label classification module and a carefully designed strategy for handling multi-class and single-label cases. It achieves a top accuracy of 42.2% on the database, significantly outperforming alternative methods.

Hyperspherical and hyperbolic graph convolutions have been developed to accommodate the curved geometry of note connections and to incorporate inductive learning into graph convolutional networks (GCNs). Building upon these developments, our research extends hyperbolic learning to Euclidean settings and introduces a novel Lorentzian graph convolutional network (LGCN) based on the Minkowski space. LGCN utilizes a unique node representation that provides both a Euclidean and a hyperbolic projection, offering an implicit link between these two spaces and a more comprehensive understanding of node characteristics. Our method offers the following key benefits: 1) it provides a more intuitive hyperbolic representation of graph data by incorporating a Euclidean component, yielding improved performance; 2) it delivers a straightforward and interpretable node representation that facilitates better generalization across various tasks; 3) it delivers a comprehensive analysis of data distribution in a mixed Euclidean-Hyperbolic space through a Euclidean component that facilitates clearer visualization and interpretation; 4) it produces an explicit implicit link between node features in different spaces through a Euclidean component that yields a more intuitive hyperbolic representation; 5) it offers a straightforward and effectiveinductive learning by incorporating a Euclidean component. Our component can also be applied to existing hyperbolic models to enhance their performance. This study examines the invertibility of a linear second-order elliptic operator with unknown diffusion and potential components in a spatial domain, given boundary measurements at the boundaries and within the sub-region. The experiment is conducted by applying a known value on the boundary, and the goal is to determine unknown components based on the resulting response and additional data. The proof of observability, as well as the stability of the inverse problem, is demonstrated. The key evidence for observability is obtained from a unique continuity equation, while Tihonov regularization is utilized for further analysis.

To understand the limitations of $ \nu$-calculus, we extend it with data to assess its complexity, an analysis that demonstrates its equivalence to first-order logic and FC0, and increases it from EComplete to signal-deterministic-SCC-complete.

Can social interactions be used to explain the mysterious behavior of subatomic particles described by the Tsallis distribution? This study aims to do just that, focusing on two key issues: how the Kadanoff-Baym equation relates to the Tsallis distribution through kinetic equilibration, and what social rules or norms correspond to the equilibration temperature found in experiments with hadrons. To address these challenges, a computer simulation called a social cellular automaton was created, modeling a one-dimensional environment where particles move and collide, much like they do in high-energy experiments. This simulation, set within the framework of special relativity, was then used to analyze how the social system evolves over time, comparing its behavior to that of a relativistic gas that follows the Tsallis distribution. The results from this simulation also led to the derivation of a 'social temperature' and revealed how the 'chemical potential' of the distribution depends on the relationship between the equilibration temperature and the new chemical temperature.

For any signed graph $H$ and a group $\mathcal{G}$, an extended $\mathcal{G}$-double cover of $H$ is defined as a $\mathcal{G}$-labeling on the edges of a graph that resembles $H$ in its connectivity pattern. This paper investigates the properties of extended double covers, focusing on their coloring and structural aspects. In the first part, sufficient conditions are set to verify the extendability of $\mathbb{Z}_3$-labelings, thereby proving Vasil'ev's conjecture, which states that nearly all extended $\mathbb{Z}_3$-double covers of signed graphs are planar. Moreover, the extendability of $\mathbb{Z}_3$-labelings is also examined for specific graphs, with particular emphasis on the complete graph $K_5$. We break down the behavior of quantum equilibrium conditions into four main groups of Hamiltonian dynamics: those showing smooth changes, those with sharp alterations, those with minor obstacles, and those with major obstacles. This classification is based on the complexity of unitary evolution and quantum singularities that result from it. For each group, we provide specific examples of solvable and inherently intricate systems, demonstrating how conditions for a lack of quantum singularities can be avoided. Furthermore, we show that the absence of quantum singularities is not necessary for equidistribution in systems with obstacles, as long as the obstacles are small. This finding is demonstrated through two distinct Hamiltonians: one with a substantial quantum barrier but equidistributes in both classical and quantum domains, and another with equidistribution in both domains, equidistributed in the Heisenberg picture, despite having an insurmountable quantum barrier. This is achieved by choosing a particular type of interaction and comparing the quantum and classical barriers.

The concept of negative temperature can be effectively illustrated through a system with two distinct energy levels. Traditionally, negative temperature is associated with systems having a large number of microstates between the two energy levels. However, within this study, a unique scenario is presented where the simpler system's entropy behavior mimics that of a system exhibiting a negative temperature regime. The distinctiveness of this approach lies in its reliance on geometric properties in phase space to represent states of the two energy levels. Utilizing this method, the existence of a negative temperature regime for the two-level system becomes evident. Furthermore, the connection to an explicit model and the connection to a physical device make the two-level system's negative temperature regime more tangible.

A general framework is established to represent A_h using components, a framework particularly useful for analyzing the structure of A_h when h is small relative to d. These relative comparisons become easier to understand through the lens of A_2 when considering even numbers of terms in the signed sum. This project aims to explore and automate the detection, classification, and sub-classification of precancerous colorectal adenomas using high-quality optical coherence tomography images through a single-stage unified neural network. Initially, the contours of the images are extracted using an open-source tool, Snappy. Following this, a unified neural network based on U-Net architecture is employed for a subsequent 2-fold adaptive pooling process to accomplish image segmentation, layer classification, and sub-classification simultaneously. Notably, this study stands out as a pioneering study in the field of medical imaging by utilizing a comprehensive dataset consisting of 10 labeled data points per image, thereby enabling accurate classification and sub-classification of the colorectal layers.

This study offers an innovative numerical solution for time-harmonic acoustic scattering in unbounded domains with varying material properties. We propose a high-frequency methodology based on local time-domain finite element methods and semi-discrete energy estimates. This framework eliminates the need for artificial boundaries, naturally enforcing the outgoing wave condition at infinity. The method translates to very stable $O(h^{-1})$ energy estimates in the time domain, bypassing the high-frequency problems commonly associated with hybrid FEM-PO methods. We implement our approach using COMSOL and MATLAB software, and provide comparative studies at multiple high frequencies. These studies demonstrate the method's performance relative to the conventional h-dependent Mesh Discretization (h-MDD) technique.

Our laboratory analysis of 50g of processed rock from the Antarctic find 1987 AA (approximately 3.4kg, discovered in Antarctica on January 28, 1987 near the Adélie Land station at coordinates 67^\circ28'S 149^\circ20'E) included measurements of water content, iron content in the form of total soluble ions, and a size-frequency distribution of embedded meteorites. The water content in this meteorite exceeded the water content found in the recently fallen ordinary chondrite meteorites Benenitra and Chelyabinsk by a significant margin, with 1987 AA containing 0.008wt\%, 1987 AA's embedded meteorites mirrored a power law curve with a slope of -2.35, and its iron content in the form of FeSO4 was found to be 0.22wt\%.

This paper builds upon a previous study and extends the analysis of forms related to matrix elements of local operators in an integrable higher-spin XXZ chain. By leveraging lower-spin representations, connections to previous work on scattering amplitudes and wave functions are confirmed. Additionally, new insights are gained through the examination of scalar product relationships, form behavior under spin exchange, asymptotic limits, and negation of imaginary variables.

A new approach to scattering problems with spherical symmetry is presented, which uses multipoles. Unlike traditional methods, this approach only addresses issues specific to the problem being solved. It is shown that electric and magnetic multipoles of any order have equal value in describing a scattering and can be used to create simple, closed-form expressions for the multipoles. These expressions represent the projection of an incoming plane wave and can be calculated directly without recursion, using an explicit formula. This explicit formula is based on Bessel functions and can be used to derive the asymptotic multipoles, providing the basis for the approach. This is supported by theoretical derivation as well as numerical confirmation. This confirms the previous conclusion that all multipoles of a given order contribute equally to the scattering and validates the effectiveness of describing multipoles with an explicit formula.

We demonstrate a connection between Schur elements and shifted Schur polynomials through a particular realization of the Harish-Chandra isomorphism. Furthermore, we establish a link between Schur elements and double Stieltjes polynomials via shifted Chebychev polynomials. This link can be expressed in terms of Macdonald polynomials at a specific specialization. A connection between double Stieltjes and Schur elements, originating from the fundamental relation between Macdonald and Schur polynomials, is derived.

We apply a small dark sector to address issues with dark parity symmetry in a parity-violating seesaw framework, allowing for a stable vacuum and reliable dark baryogenesis without cold dark matter. We study the impact of two new scalars and fermions, with small symmetrical interactions, on dark baryogenesis, vacuum stability, and dark matter abundance, and find viable parameter ranges in both scenarios.

Researchers have conducted a comprehensive study of spin-orbit coupling in transition metal oxides using a theoretical model. The model is based on a detailed analysis of first-principles data and effectively incorporates complex factors such as electron interaction and material specificity. The resulting model Hamiltonians for four 3d transition metal oxides are presented, and the researchers demonstrate the limitations of the single-particle model. The theoretical findings are validated through a comparison with DFT results. The study also highlights the significance of certain energy levels and discusses the implications of the results.

We determine the relationships between $I$-functions of toric complete intersections by expressing their $I$-functions in terms of a base model. Specifically, we focus on the case where a toric complete intersection is composed of distinct smooth divisors, utilizing exact sequences of orbifold Cohomological Hall Series to derive these relationships. By perpetuating the reduction process, we create a framework that allows us to formulate $I$-functions for any toric complete intersection in terms of a set of fundamental building blocks.

Multidimensional data visualization is a crucial aspect of business intelligence, allowing users to extract valuable insights from complex datasets. While legacy tools like OLAP and spreadsheet applications have facilitated basic data analysis, they lack flexibility and interactivity for deeper visualizations. Our research team developed a cutting-edge visualization system called ViDaExpert, an AI-driven web dashboard that leverages Natural Language Processing to automatically design and refine multidimensional visualizations in response to user queries. At the core of ViDaExpert is a set of expert rules and an interactive negotiation mechanism enabled by reinforcement learning, enabling the system to refine its visualization suggestions based on user feedback. Through a series of comparative experiments, ViDaExpert demonstrated superior performance in producing effective and user-friendly visualizations when guided by user feedback and interactivity features.

This study develops an efficient and straightforward method for solving time-dependent diffusion equations with a high-order monomial approximation in two dimensions. By approximating the spatial distribution of a function over a mesh element using a scattered set of sample points, this approach applies a finite difference scheme in time and eliminates the need for traditional finite difference, volume, or element methods. Unlike Gaussian quadrature, a simple and fast way to handle the resulting system of equations is the nearest neighbor algorithm. On a grid of nearly 10^6 points, the method achieves a solution rate of about 10^5 operations, making it possible to process large datasets in a short amount of time. By taking advantage of the irregular arrangement of points, the method can be efficiently parallelized with minimal overhead.
